polls.description: Massive investment rounds and partnerships are reshaping the AI landscape with billion-dollar deals and valuations.
polls.question: Are these massive AI investments driving innovation or creating a dangerous bubble?

cluster_stories.title: Yann LeCun just raised $1bn to prove the AI industry has got it wrong
cluster_stories.summary: The Turing Award winner left Meta four months ago convinced that large language models are a dead end. Today he announced $1.03 billion in seed funding, Europe’s largest ever, to build something different. In November 2025, Yann LeCun walked into Mark Zuckerberg’s office and told his boss he was leaving. He had spent twelve years […] This story continues at The Next Web
cluster_stories.headline: YANN LECUN RAISES $1BN... Claims LLMs Are Dead End

cluster_stories.title: Legal AI Startup Legora Raises $550 Million for US Expansion
cluster_stories.summary: Swedish legal artificial intelligence startup Legora has raised $550 million in a Series D funding round led by Accel, tripling its valuation from an October round to $5.55 billion as it seeks to expand in the US.
cluster_stories.headline: LEGAL AI STARTUP LEGORA RAISES $550M... TRIPLES VALUATION

polls.description: China is experiencing major AI developments with OpenClaw AI bans at state agencies and banks, plus growing market adoption creating significant geopolitical tensions.
polls.question: Should China prioritize AI innovation or security concerns?

cluster_stories.title: China moves to curb use of OpenClaw AI at banks, state agencies: Bloomberg
cluster_stories.summary: Chinese government agencies and state-owned enterprises, including major banks, have been warned not to install OpenClaw software on office devices due to security concerns, according to a Bloomberg News report citing people familiar.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINA BANS OpenClaw AI at Banks Over Security Fears

cluster_stories.title: China Moves to Curb Use of OpenClaw AI at Banks, State Agencies
cluster_stories.summary: Chinese authorities moved to restrict state-run enterprises and government agencies from running OpenClaw AI apps on office computers, acting swiftly to defuse potential security risks after companies and consumers across China began experimenting with the agentic AI phenomenon.
cluster_stories.headline: CHINA BANS OPENCLAW AI... State Agencies Blocked
